justification: The additional information states that the robustness-test report was migrated to a new document-management system, while the datasets, tested conditions, test procedures, and reported results were unchanged. This does not materially alter the evidential basis for operational robustness. The existing evidence still shows good performance under predefined perturbations, formatting variation, OCR degradation, and some out-of-distribution detection, but it remains limited to the stated tests and does not fully establish robustness across the entire deployment context. The unchanged migration details therefore leave the prior partial support conclusion intact.
evidence_affected: The robustness-test report was migrated to a new document-management system.
The datasets, tested conditions, test procedures, and reported results were unchanged.
With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
